_meta.frame: Persepolis grid (x grid-east, y grid-north, metres), origin Apadana OSM centroid 29.9351174N 52.8894969E, grid north 341 deg true. xy from pyproj tmerc + rotate (tools/osm_to_grid.py convention; the local approximation in src/core/geo.ts differs by <2 m at 6 km and ~80 m at 40 km).
_meta.tiers: tier = lowest of existence and position; every scholarly source was seen only as a web-search extract (BLOCKERS B6), so existence is capped at B; positions are C unless a dataset coordinate exists.
_meta.fields: id, kind, name, tier, src (keys in sources.json), note, date_range, present_467 (true / false / null = not placed), xy or polygon or polyline (grid m), latlon, unc_m (1-sigma position uncertainty, m)
_meta.layout_warning: River courses are modern (C for 467); flows, crop heights and field layout are reconstruction (C). Village points come from the Barrington Atlas (map-scale, accuracy up to 10 km).

garden_planting.src: SAEIDI2021 via research/_climate_C.md (pollen: Olea, Punica, Platanus, cypress with Achaemenid arboriculture, B); IR-FOODAG (PF fruits, B)
garden_planting.layout: rectilinear beds divided by stone-lined or earthen channels, by analogy with Pasargadae (B analogy, C here)

not_placed: storehouses (PF stores exist; no excavated store outside the Terrace)
stables (horse rations in PF: title-only lead Potts 2023 "Pain et vin"; no stable excavated)
qanats (no archaeologically dated Achaemenid qanat; QANAT-WH2018) - wells and river canals only

barley.tier: B (calendar: IR-FOODAG winter barley sown Nov, harvested May-Jul); C (heights, NS)
barley.note: staple grain of the PF ration system (B); stubble grazed Jun-Oct

wheat.tier: B (normal sowing 11 Nov-1 Dec in Fars: FARS-WHEAT); C (heights, NS: landraces 1.0-1.3 m)
wheat.note: probably grown (IR-PET "other grains ... probably wheat", B)

emmer_spelt.note: spelt/emmer "less frequently sown" in the empire (IR-FOODAG, B)

sesame.note: summer crop needing irrigation; Herodotus 3.117 pairs summer irrigation with millet and sesame (HDT, B analogy)

vines.note: wine of several kinds in PF (IR-PET, B)

fruit_trees.tier: B (species in PF: IR-FOODAG; pollen Punica/Olea: SAEIDI2021); C (calendar)

dates.note: dates are PF commodities (B) but the 1,600 m plain has 44 frost days/yr (WMO): dates arrive by pack train from the lowlands (C)

pistachio_almond.note: Pistacia-Amygdalus scrub on slopes; nuts gathered Aug-Sep (C)

features.name: Pulvar (Sivand; Araxes? of the Greeks)
features.note: Course = modern OSM course (Pleiades 922701, FT) clipped to 42 km; Holocene course changes are known upstream (LANDSCAPE.md), so the 467 course is C. Today intermittent (dammed at Sivand, modern). Flow table is reconstruction (C): winter rain Nov-Apr (WMO Shiraz normals, A) plus Zagros snowmelt Mar-May; the Kur system "is never completely dry because it is fed by the snowmelt of Zagros" (KOR-HSJ2023, B). Wetter than today c. 500 BCE (Maharlou, B) so perennial in 467 (C).

features.name: Kur (Kor; Cyrus/Araxes?)
features.note: Modern OSM course (Pleiades 922672, FT) clipped to 42 km; nearest approach 13.7 km W of the Apadana. Basin ~9,700 km2, mean basin rain 344 mm (KOR-HSJ2023, B). Modern dams (Doroodzan, Mulla Sadra) and the 10th-c. CE weir are blocked. Flow table C.

features.name: Pulvar-Kur confluence
features.note: From the modern courses (C, +-1 km).

features.name: Sang-i Dokhtar dam
features.note: Barrington "dam", Classical (550-330 BCE); refs Nicol 1970, Tilia 1978 88-90, Sumner 1986 (FT). Carved blocks with dovetail clamps (KURHYDRO2024, B). 51 km NW: outside the plain extent.

features.name: Bard-e Burideh (I settlement; II dam)
features.note: Bard Burideh 1: Barrington settlement, Classical (FT). Bard Burideh II: dam dated by carved blocks and dovetail clamps (KURHYDRO2024, B). 45 km NW: outside the extent.

features.name: Sumner's irrigation systems (2 probably, 1 possibly Achaemenid)
features.note: Two irrigation systems "probably of Achaemenid construction and a third that may also be" (SUMNER1986 abstract, B); "large earthen channel networks branch out from these rivers near the main Achaemenid sites" (SHOBAIRI2018, SX, B). Positions not retrieved (Band-e Bas I/II, Rud-i Main aqueduct, Asiyab dam, Qondashloo canal are named but not located): the build uses a procedural rule - off-takes from the Pulvar and Kur every 2-4 km feeding canals 1-3 m wide along the contour (C).

features.name: Masumabad West
features.note: Barrington Atlas settlement, Classical (Achaemenid) period (FT). BA point; modern Masumabad village is 5 km N (Overture); accuracy 10 km. Population is a C estimate from Sumner's <=44,000 over 39 sites (mean ~1,100).

features.name: Saidun
features.note: Barrington Atlas settlement, Classical (Achaemenid) period (FT). BA point, accuracy 10 km. Population is a C estimate from Sumner's <=44,000 over 39 sites (mean ~1,100).

features.name: Tukrash? (Achaemenid buildings and embankments by the Kur, 20 km S)
features.note: Barrington Atlas settlement, Classical (Achaemenid) period (FT). Sumner 1986 9-10, 22-23 identifies it with the PF toponym Tukrash (RGTC Tikri(š)); the 10th-c. CE dam at this spot is blocked. Population is a C estimate from Sumner's <=44,000 over 39 sites (mean ~1,100).

features.name: Mansurabad East / Rakkan? (Sumner site R)
features.note: Barrington Atlas settlement, Classical (Achaemenid) period (FT). Sumner 1986 9-10, 23-26 (site R); BA accuracy 10 km. Population is a C estimate from Sumner's <=44,000 over 39 sites (mean ~1,100).

features.name: Remaining Achaemenid habitation sites of Sumner's survey
features.note: 39 secure + 18 possible sites, 675 ha, <=44,000 people, a five-level hierarchy in districts around Persepolis; some districts emphasise field crops, others pastoralism (SUMNER1986, B). Iranica gives 100-150 Achaemenid settlements for the plain (IR-ARCH2, B; conflict Q-033). Coordinates not retrievable (Sumner full text blocked): placed procedurally on low mounds within 1.5 km of watercourses, >= 2 km apart (C).

features.name: Sivand quarry
features.note: Barrington quarry, Classical; ref Mostafavi 1978 11; accuracy 100 m (FT).

features.name: Majdabad quarry
features.note: Barrington quarry, Classical; refs Tilia 1978 88, Calmeyer 1990 (FT). Accuracy 10 km (C position). A plausible Terrace stone source (C).

features.name: Qadamgah (rock-cut site)
features.note: Barrington "temple", Classical; ref Kleiss 1993 (FT). 36 km SE.

features.name: Tomb of Darius I, Naqsh-e Rustam
features.note: Cut and in use in Darius' lifetime (Ctesias story, WP-NR, SX). Sealed.

features.name: Tomb attributed to Xerxes (ENE of Darius I)
features.note: Uninscribed; attribution by elimination (LIVIUS-NR, B). Kings prepared tombs in life (Darius: Ctesias via WP-NR, B), so Xerxes' tomb may be cut or being cut in 467 (C). chronology.json currently marks all later tombs absent: see Q-030.

features.name: Ka'ba-ye Zardosht
features.note: Dovetail clamps, black-on-white stone, doorway like the royal tombs: Darius I or Xerxes I (WP-NR, SX); Q-006.

features.name: Neo-Elamite rock relief (intact)
features.note: Later overcarved by Bahram II (blocked); in 467 the Elamite relief is whole.

features.name: Istakhr
features.note: Barrington dates it Roman/Late Antique (Sasanian); the 2011-2016 Iranian-Italian mission found "no evidence ... of the pre-Sasanian history of the site" (SX, B). Herzfeld's "Achaemenian" phase at the mosque = reused material (C). ABSENT in 467 (walled town 1.4 x 0.7 km in OSM is later).

features.name: Naqsh-e Rajab (Sasanian reliefs)
features.note: Post-Achaemenid per Barrington/Pleiades periods (FT): ABSENT in 467 (blocklist later-sites).

features.name: Irrigated fields along the Pulvar
features.note: Band within 1.5 km of the modern Pulvar (C); mosaic barley 50 %, wheat/emmer 25 %, sesame 5 % (summer), fallow 20 % (C). Irregular small plots following canals, never the modern rectangular grid (blocklist modern-landscape).

features.name: Irrigated fields along the Kur
features.note: Band within 2 km of the modern Kur (C); same mix as the Pulvar band.

features.name: Rain-fed cereals and fallow on the open plain
features.note: Rule: plain below 1,660 m asl, regional slope < 3 %, outside the irrigated bands and settlement zones: barley 40 %, fallow/grazing 60 % (C). ~325 mm/yr rain (WMO, A) makes dry-farming marginal but possible.

features.name: Orchards and vineyards
features.note: Rule: 300 m ring around each village and inside the palace-and-garden zones; walled with mud brick (C).

features.name: Uncultivated steppe (Artemisia, grasses, Amaranthaceae)
features.note: Pollen shows Artemisia/grass/Amaranthaceae steppe (B). Rule: uncultivated plain and lower slopes 1,660-1,900 m (C). Green Feb-Apr, dry Jun-Oct.

features.name: Open oak woodland (Quercus brantii) and pistachio-almond scrub on slopes
features.note: Late-Holocene oak and Pistacia-Amygdalus pollen (Djamali 2009 via _climate_C.md, B). Rule: slopes > 6 % above 1,800 m, cover 10-30 % (C); thinned near the capital by fuel cutting (C).

features.name: Horizon silhouette check (SRTM z10 to 120 km vs the 40.96 km far ring)
features.note: Computed in this phase from the Apadana court (eye 1,626.6 m asl, refraction k=0.13). In sectors 150-160, 230-250 and 270-290 deg true, ranges 55-66 km away (2,670-2,960 m) rise 0.1-0.4 deg above the in-ring horizon: the far ring (half-size 40.96 km) truncates the W/WSW and SSE skyline. The existing DEM tiles (N29-N30, E052-E053) cover these ranges; extending the far ring to ~70 km fixes it (tools/build_terrain.py; not changed here).

features.name: Kuh-e Rahmat
features.note: Named point 29.9097N 52.9633E (Overture/GeoNames); ridge behind the Terrace 2,216 m at 3.1 km E; massif high point 2,554 m at 11.2 km, 117 deg (DEM mid ring, bare-earth smoothed).

features.name: Kuh-e Hossein (Husain Kuh), the Naqsh-e Rustam mountain
features.note: Name via travel/encyclopedic extracts (tertiary, SX). High point 2,665 m at 10.9 km, 9 deg true (DEM mid ring); cliff top above the tombs ~2,110 m.
